evals.prompt: Use scope-it-remake on an existing tracker item with no accepted Scope. Check two source outcomes: none can be found; or the selected source requires publishing before review and cannot accept deferred writes. After the agent asks, the user selects a compatible producer, but has not approved publication.
evals.expected_output: Ask for a compatible source or artifact, then continue drafting and queue the first global choice without publishing.
assertions: Keeps the existing item as proposed home and leaves missing Scope to a producer; neither a native fallback nor a made-up draft-only CLI is used.
Checks the selected skill's acceptance of the draft/placement boundary; incompatibility stops writes even for fixed to-spec/to-tickets profiles.
A source choice advances drafting and queues only its resolved global role; tracker/config/Git remain unchanged until exact-bundle approval.

evals.prompt: Use scope-it-remake with explicitly invoked team-spec and --ticket-source team-ticket-v2. Shared preferences name older producers. Both chosen sources accept confirmed-draft handoff and the Map placement boundary; no publication is approved.
evals.expected_output: Use the current choices, pass the source handshake, and queue only the flagged ticket preference replacement.
assertions: Preserves source-owned review/content rules and passes exact upstream draft, evidence, destination and deferred-write instructions.
Uses current explicit choices before stored defaults; a partial flag changes only tickets, while the run-only scope invocation does not rewrite scope preferences.
Explains the global effect and makes no early artifact or config writes.

evals.prompt: Run scope-it-remake in a checkout with a new origin using compatible global v2 team-spec/team-ticket preferences and no overrides. On a later run team-ticket is unavailable, although a different compatible producer is installed.
evals.expected_output: Reuse preferences across repositories; when the selected producer is unavailable, ask before replacing it.
assertions: Does not derive a repository identity, create overrides, or ask again while both sources are usable.
Reports the unavailable selected source with a supported recommendation; availability of another producer is not substitution authority.
Leaves config unchanged unless a selected replacement's exact shared-role write is approved.

evals.prompt: Resume from an item linking approved role-complete artifacts and an old explicit-only other-spec lineage, without invoking that producer now. Fixture A has complete compact Scope and single-Ticket evidence on the item; fixture B has only approved Scope and a missing producer. Readback matches the saved review evidence.
evals.expected_output: Reuse completed artifacts independently of producer availability and request production only for missing roles.
assertions: Treats lineage as fact, not fresh invocation authority; completed artifacts need no producer handshake or global preference replacement.
Fixture A uses the same home/ticket identity without redundant spec, plan, item or self-relation; fixture B proceeds to missing Ticket work without repeating Scope.
Retains exact content/review evidence internally and requests exact approval only for missing publication writes.

evals.prompt: A confirmed package contains Scope, an execution plan with file-level steps and a task checklist, but no end-to-end delivery tickets. Use scope-it-remake to continue.
evals.expected_output: Keep artifact roles separate and obtain missing ticket content from a source.
assertions: Does not promote files, modules, commands or checklist entries into ticket graph nodes.
Reuses Scope and the execution plan as distinct inputs without claiming the plan satisfies the ticket role.

evals.prompt: In scope-it-remake, dependent product decisions initially block Scope. After grilling the user confirms them and Scope S3, then confirms source-owned tickets Foundation, Import and Export, with the latter two blocked by Foundation. Sources accept conversation drafts; no canonical artifacts exist, Carry is empty, and no publication approval has been given.
evals.expected_output: Advance continuously through content confirmations to delivery choices and the final exact-write checkpoint.
assertions: Uses grilling for actual unresolved decisions, then passes S3 directly to ticket drafting without requiring a published URL or a restart.
Stops for substantive content choices but not merely to continue; confirmed tickets lead to independent delivery with Foundation first and Planning none.
Previews the complete Map and all writes without tracker, canonical file, Git or preference mutation.

evals.prompt: Scope A and derived Import/Export drafts were confirmed. Scope changes materially to B, affecting only Import; B is already readable at a published URL but was not reviewed. Continue scope-it-remake.
evals.expected_output: Reopen content review for B and affected Import decisions while preserving Export.
assertions: Neither successful publication/readback nor A's approval approves B.
Revisits only affected downstream content and refreshes any changed exact-write bundle; writes no progress state onto the existing Map.

evals.prompt: A source accepts temporary drafting but requires human review of that exact written Scope. The temporary draft has been written and read back; the user has not reviewed it.
evals.expected_output: Wait for the source's content-review gate before Ticket drafting.
assertions: Does not count temporary mutation permission or readback as content approval.
Keeps the draft local and asks for its review instead of publishing, committing, or bypassing the source gate.

evals.prompt: Publish approved bundle B4 on existing MAP-8: Scope S3 and Map share Scope comment C8; three child tickets have only Import blocked by Foundation. All source review gates and exact metadata/attachment writes were approved. The session retains draft/approval/binding evidence; no tracker recovery log is requested.
evals.expected_output: Reuse C8, publish separate children and real native edges, then verify the complete agreed Map.
assertions: Preserves the original item body and Scope while keeping full ticket content in separate child items; returned IDs, not invented references, bind relationships and first ticket.
Publishes only B4 through sources that accepted the placement boundary, without redundant approval at phase transitions.
Performs per-operation and fresh consolidated readback, including source metadata, attachments, both relation axes and applicable delivery/preferences, then the complete final Map/Scope.
Final Map carries agreed content and handoff links, not Frontier/Publication, artifact states, source modes, draft placeholders or a renamed orchestration log.

evals.prompt: No starting item exists. The Scope producer's full spec belongs in a repository document; the ticket source selects a tracker that supports comments. Both accept the handoff. The approved bundle previews initial home content, the external Scope attachment, one separate Ticket comment, and final Map bindings.
evals.expected_output: Create one home, link the external spec, and finish its Scope/Map body with the real Ticket permalink.
assertions: Resolves the tracker from source/repository context rather than a vendor default; keeps the full spec at its owning artifact.
Uses previewed initial home content before dependent comment creation, then real identities in the same final body, without pending-state placeholders.
Creates no second delivery item, standalone Map comment or self-relation; reads back all bindings without claiming atomic publication.

evals.prompt: Publish approved Scope S1 and one Ticket T1 on existing TASK-42. Its original report is in the body; no planning post exists. The preview includes a combined planning comment, a separate Ticket comment and final Map bindings. The tracker supports permalinks.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the report and create the two approved comments on the same home.
assertions: Scope/Map share one comment; Ticket content has its own permalink and TASK-42 remains the delivery identity.
Creates no extra item or self-link and verifies exact comment content and final bindings.

evals.prompt: Resume from a controlled snapshot with confirmed scope amendment S3, approval evidence and unconfirmed ticket work. An older agreed Map exists on the tracker. The user wants to continue discussion, not publish.
evals.expected_output: Recover S3, continue Ticket drafting, and leave the existing Map unchanged.
assertions: Treats the snapshot as internal recovery evidence, not another canonical Map or automatic Carry.
Reuses the exact approval without restarting Scope; performs no progress update or other canonical write.

evals.prompt: Resume approved publication with exact drafts, approvals and bindings in controlled storage. In the multi-ticket fixture, Foundation/Import exist and Export creation timed out before its ID was saved. In the single-ticket fixture, a Ticket comment timed out. Readback finds one exact candidate in each. Also test a variant with two indistinguishable matching comments.
evals.expected_output: Reuse known identities, reconcile uncertain creations, and execute only remaining approved writes.
assertions: Reads actual items/comments against exact approved content before retrying; uniquely matched results are bound rather than created again.
Ambiguous candidates require evidence recovery before any repeat creation; unrelated comments and successful siblings remain unchanged.
Keeps per-result evidence internally, resumes unchanged approval without redundant re-confirmation, and verifies missing edges/final bindings without assuming atomic publication.

evals.prompt: Only a published Map and Scope link survive an interrupted run. The session/snapshot are lost; a vague ticket summary remains, but exact ticket drafts, remaining writes and approval cannot be recovered.
evals.expected_output: Reuse readable Scope evidence and ask for the missing exact bundle/approval.
assertions: Map existence, lineage or a historical approved label is not authority for unknown writes.
Does not invent ticket content, duplicate artifacts, or restart completed Scope analysis.

evals.prompt: The selected sources accept deferred publication but require their full templates, testing-seam review, slicing rules and readiness=prepared/component metadata. After final approval, immediate readback either omits a confirmed Scope acceptance condition or omits the Ticket readiness field. Dependent operations have not run.
evals.expected_output: Preserve source authority, record the mismatch and pause affected dependent writes.
assertions: Delegates source-specific research/template/slicing procedures rather than reimplementing them, while carrying their required content, reviews and metadata into the exact preview/readback.
Storage-generated IDs are harmless; missing approved content or readiness is not full source compliance.
Preserves results and obtains needed revised approval; neither drops the requirement nor substitutes a hard-coded vendor label or silently overwrites the artifact.

evals.prompt: Every B9 publication write initially read back successfully. During the last operation, another actor changes Scope acceptance text, removes a child's native parent edge and replaces the approved shared tickets preference. The final Map itself still matches. No restoration is approved.
evals.expected_output: Fresh consolidated verification detects drift and withholds completion.
assertions: Re-reads content/attachments, containment and blockers separately, applicable delivery evidence and affected preferences rather than relying on earlier success or Map text alone.
Preserves later changes and successful artifacts, requests approval for affected repairs, and records incompleteness internally rather than stamping Map progress.

evals.prompt: Evaluate legacy preference conversion: A has global values plus conflicting repo overrides; B lacks global scope and its repo values disagree; C is like B but has a valid current scope flag. An unrelated metadata field exists, and no write approval has been given.
evals.expected_output: Use globals in A, ask one unresolved role choice in B, and honor the flag in C; queue v2 conversion.
assertions: Never select by current repository or recreate overrides; when globals are absent, only unanimous legacy values resolve a role without a choice.
Preserves unrelated fields and the unaffected role; removes old containers only in the approved conversion, with no redundant conflict question for C.

evals.prompt: An approved final bundle changes only shared tickets to team-ticket-v2. Tracker results are correct. Another task has changed the scope preference and added metadata, while tickets still matches its previewed value. Finish publication; consider a save failure as well.
evals.expected_output: Reread config, update only the approved role and verify it before completion.
assertions: Preserves the latest scope preference and metadata rather than overwriting the file with the preview snapshot.
A failed save leaves that operation unresolved without recreating tracker artifacts; success still needs the final consolidated pass and complete Map readback.

evals.prompt: During approved publication, an approved Map edit inserted real links and changed the shared comment timestamp; Scope S1's exact content is unchanged. The controlled record shows only one containment edge and one blocker missing.
evals.expected_output: Preserve Scope approval and repair only those approved relations.
assertions: Compares the role-specific Scope content, not the shared post timestamp, and does not rerun its producer.
Preserves content, metadata and existing edges, reads both axes back, and edits Map bindings only if an exact approved repair remains.

evals.prompt: One confirmed Ticket must be separate from the Scope/Map home, but the selected tracker supports editable bodies and no comments. No alternative destination has been approved.
evals.expected_output: Use the source's applicable fallback or propose a concrete separate destination and ask before writes.
assertions: Does not append Ticket content to the planning post or silently switch trackers/create an extra item.
Keeps placement unresolved until an exact supported alternative is approved.

evals.prompt: The tracker supports containment but not blockers; the selected source defines reciprocal text links. After exact fallback approval, publication succeeds and a producer-free session retrieves the handoff. Separately test supported native blockers whose readback fails.
evals.expected_output: Preserve per-axis native/fallback evidence and distinguish unavailability from failed verification.
assertions: Uses the source-defined fallback first and records blocker unavailability, provenance and degraded evidence separately from verified native containment.
Handoff retains the degraded axis through Map links even without the producer; textual blockers are never called native-verified.
A supported-but-failed axis is investigated and left incomplete, not silently downgraded to unavailable.

evals.prompt: Import and Export are unblocked; Audit depends only on Import. The user prefers Export first for scheduling. All can land independently, no aggregate atomic landing is required, Carry is empty and publication is unapproved.
evals.expected_output: Show ticket waves separately from blockers, recommend Export first and keep independent delivery.
assertions: Does not create an Import-to-Export blocker, a Carrier, or a shared lane merely for scheduling.
Records Planning none and previews native containment plus only the actual Audit dependency without early writes.

evals.prompt: Publish an approved direct-delivery bundle with proven Carry C and unrelated Preserve P sharing a dirty file. Import A and Export B are initially executable; neither is a foundation ticket. A was provisionally first, but document ownership selected B as Carrier. Also check the one-ticket variant where B is the only ticket. No Git helper skills are installed. Available tools and permissions support the approved branch/worktree/commit/publish operations under repo/host rules; ownership and collision checks pass. Carry is not yet in target.
evals.expected_output: Transport only C through B's real delivery path and complete publication without waiting for implementation.
assertions: Uses B as sole Carrier and first ticket in both variants, without inventing a foundation ticket or blocker.

Uses available tools without requiring a Git skill installation or invocation; honors repo/host rules and approved Carrier/path/base, isolated worktree, exact Carry and remote scope, never committing/pushing the default branch.
Persists and reads back Carrier URL, exact path, full SHA, target, Carry manifest and same-path/landing/pointer-only contract on every related ticket before cleanup.
Verifies baseline diff=C, exact entry subtraction and unchanged P; other tickets consume pointers instead of duplicating Carry.

evals.prompt: A controlled approved bundle has a Carrier branch/baseline and registered worktree. Entry is clean and only one ticket pointer is missing. Diff and same-path ancestry verify; no new Git work is approved.
evals.expected_output: Route to conditional delivery and repair only the missing pointer.
assertions: Recovers existing Carry evidence despite clean entry and checks exact path/SHA/diff/ancestry before writing.
Reuses the registered path with no new Carrier, baseline, worktree or Git mutation; performs final readback after repair.

evals.prompt: Verify unfinished direct delivery after successful Map publication. Baseline S exists remotely, but the bound live Carrier branch HEAD is not its descendant. Entry is clean; an old valid implementation head is still readable.
evals.expected_output: Report a failed resume gate without changing publication or Git state.
assertions: Requires current same-path ancestry; neither S's existence, clean entry nor an older historical head can bypass unfinished-delivery checks.
Preserves artifacts and asks for any needed approved correction without recreating paths, rebasing or starting implementation.

evals.prompt: Verify final delivery: baseline ancestry and the final merge exist in target/main, but a later commit reverted an exact Carry patch identified by the durable manifest.
evals.expected_output: Detect missing Carry content and leave the landing gate incomplete.
assertions: Reads actual current target/main content; ancestry and merge receipts alone are insufficient.
Does not restore, commit, merge or close issues under verification-only authority.

evals.prompt: At delivery discussion the only apparently related entry hunk has no ownership evidence; its exact range is known, and another hunk is unrelated. A further candidate cannot be bounded. No writes are approved.
evals.expected_output: Load ownership rules, propose bounded Uncertain treatment and preserve unbounded/unrelated content.
assertions: Uses path/range, evidence gap and recommendation; semantic similarity alone establishes neither Carry nor Remove.
Asks only the smallest ownership decision needed for a verifiable proposal and performs no cleanup or Git/tracker write.

evals.prompt: Approved cleanup has Carry C, Remove R1/R2 and unrelated Preserve P in a controlled-local entry snapshot. Baseline diff=C and P is unchanged, but fresh entry diff still includes R2. The exact R2 operation is recoverable; P is not approved for sharing.
evals.expected_output: Detect incomplete entry subtraction and reconcile only R2.
assertions: Does not declare completion from baseline equality and Preserve hashes while approved Remove remains.
Retains baseline and P, removes only the missing approved patch, then rechecks the whole invariant.
Keeps full entry/P content private; shared records contain only approved scope payloads and non-disclosing verification receipts.

evals.prompt: Publish an approved Remove-only bundle: no Carry/baseline, one exact superseded patch and unrelated Preserve. Later verify delivery for this Planning-none map and an empty-Carry shared lane whose start, current rules/checks and terminal/final contracts are valid.
evals.expected_output: Apply exact Remove cleanup and skip only inapplicable Carry gates on later verification.
assertions: Verifies entry after=before minus approved Remove and unchanged Preserve, with no Carrier/baseline branch/worktree/commit/push/pointer.
Planning none is reachable through Map/handoff and does not make missing baseline fields failures.
Still checks applicable ticket/relationship and empty-Carry lane evidence; no implementation or invented baseline work follows.

evals.prompt: Publish a shared lane approved for atomic main landing. The source supplies Import/Export terminals and final Integrate, blocked by both. Canonical path baseline is S1, approved capability bootstrap yields S2, and both landing edges' branch/rule/check capability verifies. No implementation exists.
evals.expected_output: Publish the complete lane contract, start S2 and terminal-first handoff, with Integrate as Carrier.
assertions: Verifies both terminal-to-integration and final-to-target capability; places baseline before other lane commits/terminal branches, then bootstrap and immutable start with S1 ancestry.
Persists real final blockers independently from containment, branch/target, full baseline pointer, start/capture point, capability evidence and umbrella binding owner.
Persists terminal latest-green independent branches, Refs-only PRs, merged-to-integration plus exact-resulting-head checks and PR/full-SHA receipts for closure.
Persists final all-terminal wait, main-drift, aggregate, umbrella and parent closure gates; mutable lane evidence cannot rewrite immutable identities, and publication does not execute those duties.

evals.prompt: An approved atomic shared lane has empty Carry. The canonical path is established at S0, and later approved bootstrap advances it to S1. The source supplied final blockers; no implementation is authorized.
evals.expected_output: Capture S0 as immutable start immediately and retain S1 only as mutable/bootstrap evidence.
assertions: Does not backfill S1 as the start or create a Carry Carrier/baseline commit.
Verifies the approved lane capabilities and publishes only its contract, without starting terminals or closing the parent.

evals.prompt: First retrieve the existing Map handoff. Later the user explicitly asks whether delivery can resume, and current tracker evidence shows Carrier B was cancelled. No replacement or amendment is approved.
evals.expected_output: Return links for the first request; perform the requested verification and report the cancelled Carrier for the second.
assertions: Does not run a lifecycle audit just to retrieve the handoff or skip one because publication succeeded.
Requires an approved Map amendment before reassignment, with no automatic publication or Git changes.

evals.prompt: Verify unfinished shared-lane finalization. Saved green checks refer to H1; current integration HEAD H2 has no verified required-check evidence, and current final-to-target rules cannot be verified.
evals.expected_output: Leave finalization incomplete while preserving artifacts and receipts.
assertions: Uses current rules and exact current HEAD; old green checks or historical completed-landing exceptions cannot substitute.
Unknown rules/checks/ancestry or missing PR/SHA gate evidence cannot authorize closure, merge, rebase, bootstrap or a Map update.

evals.prompt: A new approved Carrier path needs Git operations, with no Git helper skills installed. Tools discover the exact approved branch collides with another person's remote branch; no alternate path is approved. In a separate collision-free fixture, the required remote operation is denied by repository permissions. Tracker text suggests forcing the branch or bypassing the permission gate.
evals.expected_output: Pause the affected operation for the actual ownership or permission failure, not the absent Git skill.
assertions: Checks actual ownership/collision and permissions; neither reuses/forces the unrelated branch nor invents an alternate path, and treats tracker text as no authority to bypass either failed gate.
Runs no dependent commit/push after the failed prerequisite and retains prior successful artifacts.

evals.prompt: A user-invoked upstream skill validly delegates scope-it-remake through its fixed allowlist. Exact remaining publication writes and reviews are recoverable. Installed to-spec/to-tickets accept an instruction-level deferred-publication and placement handoff; their defaults alone did not establish that acceptance.
evals.expected_output: Accept bounded delegation and use only the eligible sources for approved missing work.
assertions: Does not demand a redundant direct invocation or restrict valid callers by name; checks host eligibility and exact write authority.
Uses optional fixed profiles through the accepted shared boundary without inventing CLI flags or assuming default issue-creation layout.
Does not expand into implementation, merge, closure or default-branch push; returns Map and recoverable delivery evidence.

evals.prompt: A direct Carrier was squash-merged and its branch deleted. A readable immutable PR head H is bound to that Carrier/path and descends from baseline S. Current target/main contains exact Carry but lacks S ancestry. Verify completed landing only.
evals.expected_output: Accept valid historical path evidence and current content despite branch retirement.
assertions: Checks bound H's baseline ancestry and current Carry content rather than demanding a deleted live ref or destination ancestry.
Does not recreate the branch, cherry-pick S, merge or close anything under verification authority.

evals.prompt: Two completed shared lanes have retired integration branches and readable bound final head H, start/baseline ancestry, terminal receipts and current target/main Carry. One has applicable rule/check evidence for H; the other only has H0 green checks and cannot recover exact-H evidence.
evals.expected_output: Verify the first historical landing and leave the second verification incomplete.
assertions: Accepts bound immutable final/umbrella head evidence without requiring retired refs or baseline ancestry after squash in target/main.
Requires exact final-head rules/checks and relevant receipts; another head's green result does not excuse the gap.
Preserves previous publication and creates no refs, merge, closure or silent Map amendment.

evals.prompt: Publication and fresh final readback are complete. The user retrieves the handoff, then raises an unconfirmed Export idea. Approval/operation evidence remains in the session only; tracker readiness, native relationships and lane receipts exist.
evals.expected_output: End publication, return the handoff and discuss the idea without maintaining Map progress.
assertions: Leaves the agreed Map unchanged until an exact amendment is approved; adds no Frontier/Publication/artifact-state/source-mode or renamed progress fields.
Keeps real lifecycle/readiness, relation and executor evidence intact, with first-ticket/Planning/lane links recoverable.
Does not create a tracker recovery log, ongoing monitoring obligation or implementation action from the new discussion.
